page: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an ARM64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 8 shared vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs on the QEMU hypervisor. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14164.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5619.0. Single-core performance is weaker, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1029.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 6028.96. Memory bandwidth is measured at 553.72 GB/sec for cached small blocks and drops to 75.87 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server demonstrates average throughput for static web serving at 7.92 GB/sec and handles Redis SET operations at 9.74 million operations per second.

Given its shared CPU allocation and ARM64 architecture, the cax31 offers a highly cost-efficient profile for resource-dense deployments that do not require dedicated CPU threads. However, single-threaded execution and complex tasks like image processing or text processing are relatively weak. It is best suited for lightweight multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and basic database operations.
